subject: New paper on HMC principles and Stan vs. JAGS

messages.author: 395bdca538bcae5d
messages.subject: New paper on HMC principles and Stan vs. JAGS
parts:
Hi all,

FYI I have a commentary paper out (here) that is geared towards ecologists accustomed to JAGS but wanting to move to Stan. I explain the principles of HMC/NUTS using simple language, illustrative examples, and minimal mathematics. I hope it will make a good primer for a lot of applied folks in other fields who want to make the jump but are confused by the HMC terminology (divergences, tree depths, etc.) and intimidated by the Stan user manual. I also do some efficiency comparisons for some difficult models in population ecology, and Stan was consistently faster.

The Stan team may be particularly interested in Fig. 1 which shows citation patterns for the BUGS family and Stan. It seems pretty clear Stan will dominate within a few years. Recreating something like Fig. 3 in the manual may also be a good idea to help introduce some of the concepts that are talked about mathematically.

Below is the BibTex citation.

Thanks to the dev team and community for all the help along the way.

Cheers,
Cole

@article {MEE3:MEE312681,
author = {Monnahan, Cole C. and Thorson, James T. and Branch, Trevor A.},
title = {Faster estimation of Bayesian models in ecology using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo},
journal = {Methods in Ecology and Evolution},
issn = {2041-210X},
url = {http://dx.doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12681},
doi = {10.1111/2041-210X.12681},
pages = {n/a--n/a},
keywords = {Bayesian inference, hierarchical modelling, Markov chain Monte Carlo, no-U-turn sampler, Stan},
year = {2016},
}
